data.narrative:
Fortera, a Series C-stage climate and energy company founded by Ryan Gilliam, has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparables universe of nine private frontier-tech firms in the same sector and stage, supplemented by one relevant public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $200M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding $340M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, same-stage comps—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—producing a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

These methods triangulate to a valuation range of $289M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $670M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in comparable valuations within the frontier-climate sector, where stage-progression mechanics suggest conservatism relative to peer-based estimates. The $1.0B peer median lies above the triangulated midpoint, driven by KoBold Metals' outlier $3.0B valuation. Key uncertainties include the appropriate peer weighting—particularly KoBold's materiality—and whether Fortera's capital efficiency and technology maturity justify positioning within the peer range or closer to stage-based progression.
